messages:
Nora Singh: FYI getting multiple urgent tickets complaining about slow responses from hosted text-gen -> customers seeing p95 from ~120ms up to ~700ms and sporadic p99s ~3s. Reports started ~2026-03-15T10:12:xxZ. Escalating to infra/SRE. :rotating_light:

Ravi Desai: seeing the same in dashboards. spike in tail latency aligns with a rollout window around 02:00 UTC this morning where we pushed nvidia-driver 536.12 + CUDA 12.3 and host kernel 6.7.1 to the new AZ pools. also ran nvme controller firmware upgrade 7.3 on some hosts.

Ellen Zhao: i've started a light repro loop hitting /v1/chat/completions (64 tokens) to reproduce locally against an affected host: 

```bash
# quick repro (single worker)
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-infra/prod/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"latency test"}],"max_tokens":64}' >/dev/null;
done
```

Ellen Zhao: on the host (gpu-eu1-07) `perf top` shows occasional CPU stalls and `nvme-cli` shows high avg latency on io stats. nvme SMART shows controller reset counters incrementing.

Kai Moreno: pulled iostat & nvme stats during repro. here's a short excerpt: 

```
Device            r/s    w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await  svctm  %util
nvme1n1          180.6  40.2  2048.0  512.0    12.0     3.4    310.2  1.9   92.1
```

Ravi Desai: also seeing gpu dma interrupts climb and kernel logs show repeated nvme timeout/abort messages. snippet from dmesg: 

```
[34567.890123] nvme nvme1: abort_cmd: status=0x4 opcode=0x1
[34567.892000] nvme_core: reset controller required
[34568.003210] kernel: pci 0000:65:00.0: BAR 0: failed to enable mem region
```

infra-bot: Created incident INC-196400 - High p95/p99 on hosted-prod / text-gen due to suspected storage-driver interaction. Severity: high. Owners: Ravi Desai, Kai Moreno.

Nora Singh: we have customers on phone, sending preliminary note: "We’re aware of elevated latency for text generation; our engineers are investigating and applying mitigations. Will update in 30 minutes."

Kai Moreno: quick mitigation options I can run now: 1) move traffic away from nodes with nvme fw 7.3 to older fw nodes 2) adjust io scheduler to none or mq-deadline on affected hosts 3) hypervisor-level PCI passthrough changes to reduce inter-run DMA overlap. moving traffic is fastest.

Ellen Zhao: I can throttle heavy embedding routes at the edge to reduce burst IO. can flip a flag in the api-gateway config to cap concurrency for embeddings to 8 per instance.

Ravi Desai: plan: 
- step 1 (10m): enable embed route throttle in gateway (Ellen)
- step 2 (20m): cordon & drain 2 suspected affected nodes and repro after moving them to driver-525 image and nvme fw 7.1 (Kai/Ravi)
- step 3: collect `fio --filename=/dev/nvme1n1 --iodepth=64 --size=1G --readwrite=randrw --bs=4k --runtime=60 --group_reporting` output, nvme logs, dmesg, lspci and nvidia-smi outputs and upload (Kai)
- step 4: vendor SR if rollback confirms causality (Ravi/Aisha)

Nora Singh: let's also prepare a small rollback playbook: minimal impact rollback steps, change window, and customer notification text. I’ll draft.

Kai Moreno: drained gpu-eu1-07, booting with driver 525.x and kernel 6.5. quick synthetic against only that node now shows p95 ~130ms and p99 ~430ms. before rollback same node had p95 ~690ms and p99 ~3.1s.

Ellen Zhao: after we re-routed some production traffic to the rolled-back node, cluster-wide p95 dropped from 700ms -> 210ms and p99s reduced to ~600-800ms. still not fully back to baseline but big improvement.

Ravi Desai: uploaded collector bundle: https://internal.artifacts.redwood/INC-196400/collectors.tar.gz includes fio, nvme logs, dmesg, kernel modules list. nvme log shows firmware reset events around the degraded window.

infra-bot: Alert: Vendor SR opened - SR-90034 with GPU driver vendor and NVMe firmware vendor. Logs attached.

Nora Singh: customer comms draft ready: "We identified an infrastructure regression impacting tail latency caused by a recent driver/firmware/kernel combination. We have initiated a rollback on affected nodes and are throttling heavy routes to reduce impact. We'll provide a full postmortem after root cause confirmed." Posting to CS-9102/CS-9103.

Kai Moreno: additional short-term mitigations we tested: 
- switching io scheduler from mq-deadline -> none reduced tail by ~30% on synthetic fio runs
- setting `nvme_core.io_timeout` higher prevented immediate resets but didn't fix latency
- disabling contiguous DMA (iommu tweaks) reduced overlap but requires reboot/hypervisor change

Ellen Zhao: note for postmortem: include reproducible script and exact kernel/driver/fw matrix, customer impact windows and tickets affected. I saved repro commands and test results to the incident folder.

Ravi Desai: let's pause any further 536.x rollouts globally until vendor confirms compatibility with NVMe FW 7.3 + kernel 6.7.1. I'll update deploy gating and create a release-block label.

Nora Singh: good work team. keep updates here. i’ll coordinate cs comms and the incident timeline. once we confirm rollback fixes we're moving to remediate and schedule a controlled revalidation with vendor. :thumbsup:
